evidence.title: Incident Report #0411-27

paragraphs: At 06:48 on April 11, a garage attendant at the Summit Ridge parking structure reported an electric sedan left on Level P3 for hours with its doors locked.

Officers opened the vehicle and found a woman, later identified as Mara Ellis, 26, a vocalist who had worked with recording artist n0va. She was pronounced dead at the scene. Cause of death is under investigation.
The sedan is leased by Halewood Management LLC, the company that represents n0va. Two digital keys are registered to it: KEY-A and KEY-B.
Mara was last known to be at n0va's recording studio. Studio A is a badge-controlled facility, and door audits are available on request.
At 09:15 the same morning, n0va's name began circulating on social media. No suspect had been named by police.

evidence.analyst_note: Two keys. One car. Somebody drove it from the studio to this garage.

evidence.title: Vehicle Telemetry Export
evidence.analyst_note: The car was driven at 02:09. The last key used was KEY-B. Not KEY-A.

evidence.title: STUDIO CREW Group Chat

lines.text: Who leaked the demo? Be honest.
Not me. I swear. I would never.
Can we not do this in the group chat?
Rex told me the song credits are changing. My name is off the track.
Rex handles that stuff. I didn't sign anything.
Then why is it in the contract draft?
Take a breath. We'll fix it tomorrow.
I'm sitting in the car. Need some air.
Sorry, I got called in to my hospital shift. Text me.

evidence.analyst_note: An argument is not an alibi problem, and it is not a crime. Who controls the contract?

evidence.title: Public Reaction Timeline

rows: n0va named by an anonymous account
Petitions ask platforms to pull n0va's songs
Fans split: guilty vs. wait for facts
Statement: no suspect has been identified

evidence.analyst_note: The public verdict arrived about 25 hours before the police statement.

evidence.title: Digital Key Registry

rows: KEY-B authorised users: R. Hale only

evidence.analyst_note: Somebody signed KEY-B out at 22:55. The registry says who.

evidence.title: Voicemail to Mara Ellis, 22:41

lines.text: Mara. It's Rex. Don't make this a scene in front of the kid. We need to talk about the contract. Tonight. Before the label call.
I'm coming to the studio. Stay where you are. And don't talk to anyone.

evidence.analyst_note: Mara never called back. Her next message went to Tessa.

evidence.title: Studio A Door Audit
evidence.analyst_note: Studio A has no side door. Nobody leaves without a badge. Where was n0va at 02:09?

evidence.title: Interview: Tessa Rowe

lines.text: St. Aurelia Hospital. I work nights as a unit clerk. They called me in.
The time clock. In at 22:52, out at 07:10. HR can pull it. I never left the building.
She texted at 22:34. 'Rex is on his way. He sounds mad.' I told her to stay put. I should have called someone.

evidence.analyst_note: Hospital HR confirmed the time clock. Tessa was never near the studio lot.

evidence.title: Studio Lot Camera Index

rows: Man in a jacket marked HALEWOOD walks to the sedan with a key fob
Sedan leaves. Driver wears the same HALEWOOD jacket
n0va visible inside the studio, at the mixing desk
Same man leaves on foot. Face match: R. Hale (94%)

evidence.analyst_note: At 02:09, one man was driving the car and another was at a mixing desk.

evidence.title: Hale Card and Payment Log
evidence.analyst_note: A ride, a prepaid phone, a lawyer. Suspicious. But none of it puts him at the car.
